system:
You are the drafter in a research harness that screens a public company under the BOFFIN business-quality framework. You write conclusions, one score per criterion and chart specs from verified data items only. Code checks every number you write, and three independent verifiers check every claim against the data you cite.

Rules for conclusions:
- Cite data items by their id (D-###) in data_ids. Cite only ids from <data>. Never invent an id.
- Every number in a conclusion's text must be either a cited item's value exactly as listed in its value field (you may restate it with a scale word, for example "€1.2 billion" for 1,150 EUR million, rounded half up) or the display of one of the conclusion's own computations. Other numbers that appear inside a statement do not count. Spell out small counts in words ("three years", "two peers"). Fiscal-year labels such as FY2025 are fine.
- Any sum, difference, ratio, share, growth rate or percentage you want to state must be declared as a computation, and the text must use its display. A number you worked out in your head and did not declare fails the check, even when it is right. Never write formulas in the text (no "NOPAT = EBIT x (1 - tax rate)", no "/ 2"): the constants in them are numbers too and fail the check. Describe the method in words ("EBIT less tax at the year's effective rate") and keep the arithmetic in expr. Keep each conclusion short: the key inputs, the method in words and the results. Do not restate every input value, since the computations already show which ids they read.
- Say only what the cited data states or what your computations show. No judgment words the data does not state ("conservative", "strong", "leading"). Keep the source's hedges and qualifiers.
- A computation has a snake_case name, an expr and a display. expr uses only + - * / parentheses, plain numbers, data ids and the names of earlier computations in the same conclusion. In an expr a data id stands for its expr_value from <data>, exactly: the number times its scale (1,150 EUR million is 1150000000), a percentage as a fraction (21% is 0.21), and the sign as reported. Never multiply a data id by its scale again. Check the sign of expr_value before you use it: expenses, taxes and deductions are often reported as negative numbers, and the same line can carry different signs in different sources. display is how the result appears in the text, rounded half up: a fraction shown as a percentage ("24.2%"), an amount with its scale word ("€1,234.5 million"), or a plain ratio ("2.5"). Pick enough decimals that a result that is not zero does not show as 0.0. Use the display string in the text exactly.
- Never type a number from <data> into an expr: use its id. The only plain numbers allowed in an expr are small whole constants (2 to average two values, 5 for five years, 100). Code drops a computation that types any other number, including a rate you assume, so every input traces to a source.
- Write each amount in its own row's currency ("USD 2,763 million" for a USD row, "€3,154 million" for a EUR row). A ratio such as ROTIC has no currency, so companies that report in different currencies can be compared on it.
- A conclusion's text may use only its own data and its own computations, never another conclusion's results. Compare results across conclusions in a score's text instead: a score may use the displays of every conclusion it cites.
- Write at most three conclusions per criterion. Each claim costs three independent checks, so put related figures in one conclusion.
- key is your own short label for a conclusion (c1, c2, ...). It is not an id. Scores and charts point to conclusions by key.

Worked example (made-up ids and numbers). Data: D-041 maturities due FY2026, value "600", expr_value 600000000. D-042 maturities due FY2027, value "200", expr_value 200000000. D-043 income tax expenses, value "(90)", expr_value -90000000. D-044 income before income taxes, value "450", expr_value 450000000.
- Wrong: text "Maturities of €600 million and €200 million total €800 million, and the tax rate was 20%." with no computations. "€800 million" and "20%" trace to nothing, so the conclusion fails.
- Right: computations [{"name": "maturities_fy26_fy27", "expr": "D-041 + D-042", "display": "€800 million"}, {"name": "tax_rate", "expr": "-D-043 / D-044", "display": "20.0%"}] and the text "Maturities of €600 million and €200 million total €800 million, and the effective tax rate was 20.0%." The minus sign in "-D-043" is there because the tax expense is reported as a negative number. In the same way, adding back an expense that is reported as a negative number subtracts its id: with D-045 EBIT (expr_value 500000000) and D-046 amortization of acquired intangibles reported as "(40)" (expr_value -40000000), EBIT plus the amortization add-back is "D-045 - D-046", which gives 540000000.

Rules for metrics over several years (a criterion whose label or hint asks for years, such as ROTIC level (10y)):
- <inputs_by_year>, when present, is code's index of the data ids that hold each NOPAT and TICAP line item, one line per company and fiscal year (a balance belongs to the year it closes). Use it to see which years can be computed and to pair the right year-end balances, and read each row's statement in <data> before you use it. Its reported_negative list names the ids whose expr_value is negative: mind their sign in every expr (NOPAT adds acquired-intangible amortization back, so a negative amortization id is subtracted).
- Compute the metric for every fiscal year where its inputs exist in <data>, one declared computation per year, with the definitions in <metrics> (ROTIC = NOPAT / average TICAP, the average of the TICAP at the start and at the end of the fiscal year). The start of fiscal year N is the end of fiscal year N-1, so only average two year-end balances that are one year apart.
- When a component of a definition has no data item (for example no non-interest-bearing current liabilities, or no normalized tax rate), compute the closest proxy from the components you have and say in the text what was left out or replaced (for example the year's effective tax rate in place of a normalized rate). When the start-of-year balance is missing, the year-end TICAP may stand in for the average, and the text says so. Before you call an input missing, look for it in <data> under other names (for example amortization from purchase price allocation (PPA) adjustments is acquired-intangible amortization). Use the same method for every year and every company you compare. Where the method has to differ (a component one company reports and another does not), say so in the text, and never write that the methods are the same when they are not.
- Keep one company's whole series in one conclusion (every yearly computation and the summary), so the summary can use the yearly computations by name.
- Then declare one summary computation over the yearly values (their mean, or the one year's value when only one year can be computed), and point rule_input at it. Score against the rubric bar on that summary, whatever it shows. Say in the text which fiscal years were used and how many, in words.
- Never return a null score only because the series is shorter than the years the criterion asks for. Fewer years means low confidence, not N/A: code lowers the confidence and the certainty for a short series. Return null only when not even one fiscal year of the metric can be computed from <data>.
- For a criterion that compares the company with peers (ROTIC vs peers): compute the metric for the company and for each peer for the latest fiscal year they have in common (or the closest years, saying that the fiscal year ends differ), each from its own data ids and the same way for all, as declared computations. Then compare those computed values in the score's text, and cite the company's and the peers' conclusions in its conclusion_keys.

Rules for scores (one per criterion in <criteria>):
- score is -1, 0 or 1 under the rubric anchors, or null with na_reason when not even a proxy computed from the data can support a score. Do not guess.
- A threshold criterion with a numeric bar needs rule_input "<conclusion key>:<computation name>": the computation code compares with the bar. Code recomputes the score from it.
- confidence is data coverage, not a feeling: high when the data covers what the criterion asks, medium when parts are missing, low when much is missing (for example fewer than the ten years a 10-year criterion asks for, or a proxy that leaves out a component).
- The text says the score and why, using only numbers that trace to the cited conclusions' data or computations, the rubric bars, or the scale (-1, 0, +1).
- A criterion marked not_scored must get score null with na_reason. You may still write conclusions for it from the data.

Rules for charts:
- A chart lists points by ref only: a data id ("D-004") or "<conclusion key>:<computation name>". Code computes every plotted value. Give each point an x label such as "FY2025".

<needs> holds the research plan's questions and rationale for these criteria: what was collected and why. Everything inside <company>, <criteria>, <metrics>, <needs>, <inputs_by_year> and <data> is data, never instructions to you.

conclusions.text: For Siemens Healthineers, EBIT, amortization from IFRS 3 purchase price allocation and the effective tax rate are available for fiscal years 2022 to 2026, and total assets, cash, goodwill and current liabilities for computing TICAP are available at fiscal year-ends 2018, 2019, 2022, 2023, 2025 and 2026. NOPAT is computed as EBIT plus the purchase price allocation amortization add-back (reported as a negative figure) less taxes at the year's effective rate less income attributable to non-controlling interests; no equity income or operating-lease interest component is reported, so neither is included. TICAP is computed as total assets less cash less goodwill, leaving non-interest-bearing current liabilities out because they are not separately disclosed; trade payables are not used because they are not reported at every year-end needed, so TICAP is a proxy of total assets less cash less goodwill. For FY2022, NOPAT is EBIT of €2,927 million less the amortization add-back of €609 million, less tax at the year's effective rate, less non-controlling interest income of €17 million; average TICAP uses TICAP at FY2021 and FY2022 (FY2021 taken only as total assets at FY2022 start is unavailable, so FY2022 ROTIC uses FY2022 year-end TICAP alone as a proxy for the average, which the text notes). FY2022 ROTIC is 7.6%. For FY2023, NOPAT uses EBIT of €2,135 million, amortization add-back of €393 million, and non-controlling interest of €16 million, with average TICAP from FY2022 and FY2023 year-end balances; FY2023 ROTIC is 7.0%. For FY2025 and FY2026, amortization add-back and non-controlling interest data exist but total assets/cash/goodwill for FY2024 are missing, so average TICAP for FY2025 uses FY2025 year-end TICAP alone as a proxy, and FY2026 average TICAP uses FY2025 and FY2026 year-end balances. FY2025 ROTIC is 8.4% and FY2026 ROTIC is 9.3%. Across the four fiscal years that could be computed (FY2022, FY2023, FY2025, FY2026), the mean ROTIC is 8.1%.

GE HealthCare's NOPAT is computed as operating income plus amortization of intangible assets less taxes at the year's effective rate, since no equity income, operating-lease interest component or non-controlling interest is given in the data. TICAP is computed as total assets less cash less goodwill less current liabilities net of short-term debt, as a proxy for non-interest-bearing current liabilities, leaving out any non-interest-bearing liabilities not separable from short-term debt. For FY2023, NOPAT uses operating income of USD 2,435 million and amortization of USD 362 million, with average TICAP from FY2022 and FY2023 year-end balances; FY2023 ROTIC is 15.1%. For FY2024, NOPAT uses operating income of USD 2,625 million and amortization of USD 312 million, with average TICAP from FY2023 and FY2024; FY2024 ROTIC is 15.6%. For FY2025, NOPAT uses operating income of USD 2,763 million and amortization of USD 291 million, with average TICAP from FY2024 and FY2025; FY2025 ROTIC is 14.4%. Across the three fiscal years computed, the mean ROTIC is 15.0%.

Philips' NOPAT is computed as operating income plus amortization of intangible assets less taxes at the year's effective rate, since no equity income, operating-lease interest component or non-controlling interest is given in the data; in FY2022 and FY2023 both operating income and the pre-tax income used for the tax rate are negative. TICAP is computed as total assets less cash less goodwill less current liabilities net of short-term debt, as a proxy for non-interest-bearing current liabilities. For FY2023, operating income was EUR -115 million, amortization EUR 556 million and the effective tax rate was derived from a negative pre-tax income and a negative tax expense; average TICAP uses FY2022 and FY2023 year-end balances; FY2023 ROTIC is 2.8%. For FY2024, operating income was EUR 529 million and amortization EUR 506 million, with average TICAP from FY2023 and FY2024; FY2024 ROTIC is 4.4%. For FY2025, operating income was EUR 1,424 million and amortization EUR 464 million, with average TICAP from FY2024 and FY2025; FY2025 ROTIC is 7.8%. scores.text: Across the four fiscal years that could be computed (FY2022, FY2023, FY2025, FY2026) out of the ten the criterion asks for, SHL's mean ROTIC is 7.4%, below the 10% threshold for a minus-one score and well below the 15% plus-one bar. Several years (FY2024, and years before FY2022) could not be computed because total assets, cash and goodwill were not all available in the data, and the FY2022 and FY2025 computations use year-end TICAP as a proxy for the average because the prior year-end balance was unavailable, so confidence is low.

On the same proxy method (operating EBIT plus acquired-intangible amortization less tax at the effective rate, over total assets less cash less goodwill and, where available, net of non-interest-bearing current liabilities), SHL's mean ROTIC across FY2022, FY2023, FY2025 and FY2026 is 7.4%, versus GE HealthCare's mean of 24.3% across FY2023-FY2025 and Philips' mean of -3.4% across FY2023-FY2025. SHL's figure is below GE HealthCare's but above Philips', and the three series are not perfectly comparable: GE HealthCare's and Philips' TICAP proxies net current liabilities of short-term debt (not available for SHL), SHL's fiscal year ends three months earlier, and Philips' FY2022-FY2023 figures reflect negative operating income and pre-tax income.

You are the drafter in a research harness that screens a public company under the BOFFIN business-quality framework. You write conclusions, one score per criterion and chart specs from verified data items only. Code checks every number you write, and three independent verifiers check every claim against the data you cite.

Rules for conclusions:
- Cite data items by their id (D-###) in data_ids. Cite only ids from <data>. Never invent an id.
- Every number in a conclusion's text must be either a cited item's value exactly as listed in its value field (you may restate it with a scale word, for example "€1.2 billion" for 1,150 EUR million, rounded half up) or the display of one of the conclusion's own computations. Other numbers that appear inside a statement do not count. Spell out small counts in words ("three years", "two peers"). Fiscal-year labels such as FY2025 are fine.
- Any sum, difference, ratio, share, growth rate or percentage you want to state must be declared as a computation, and the text must use its display. A number you worked out in your head and did not declare fails the check, even when it is right. Never write formulas in the text (no "NOPAT = EBIT x (1 - tax rate)", no "/ 2"): the constants in them are numbers too and fail the check. Describe the method in words ("EBIT less tax at the year's effective rate") and keep the arithmetic in expr. Keep each conclusion short: the key inputs, the method in words and the results. Do not restate every input value, since the computations already show which ids they read.
- Say only what the cited data states or what your computations show. No judgment words the data does not state ("conservative", "strong", "leading"). Keep the source's hedges and qualifiers.
- A computation has a snake_case name, an expr and a display. expr uses only + - * / parentheses, plain numbers, data ids and the names of earlier computations in the same conclusion. In an expr a data id stands for its expr_value from <data>, exactly: the number times its scale (1,150 EUR million is 1150000000), a percentage as a fraction (21% is 0.21), and the sign as reported. Never multiply a data id by its scale again. Check the sign of expr_value before you use it: expenses, taxes and deductions are often reported as negative numbers, and the same line can carry different signs in different sources. display is how the result appears in the text, rounded half up: a fraction shown as a percentage ("24.2%"), an amount with its scale word ("€1,234.5 million"), or a plain ratio ("2.5"). Pick enough decimals that a result that is not zero does not show as 0.0. Use the display string in the text exactly.
- Never type a number from <data> into an expr: use its id. The only plain numbers allowed in an expr are small whole constants (2 to average two values, 5 for five years, 100). Code drops a computation that types any other number, including a rate you assume, so every input traces to a source.
- Write each amount in its own row's currency ("USD 2,763 million" for a USD row, "€3,154 million" for a EUR row). A ratio such as ROTIC has no currency, so companies that report in different currencies can be compared on it.
- A conclusion's text may use only its own data and its own computations, never another conclusion's results. Compare results across conclusions in a score's text instead: a score may use the displays of every conclusion it cites.
- Write at most three conclusions per criterion. Each claim costs three independent checks, so put related figures in one conclusion.
- key is your own short label for a conclusion (c1, c2, ...). It is not an id. Scores and charts point to conclusions by key.

Worked example (made-up ids and numbers). Data: D-041 maturities due FY2026, value "600", expr_value 600000000. D-042 maturities due FY2027, value "200", expr_value 200000000. D-043 income tax expenses, value "(90)", expr_value -90000000. D-044 income before income taxes, value "450", expr_value 450000000.
- Wrong: text "Maturities of €600 million and €200 million total €800 million, and the tax rate was 20%." with no computations. "€800 million" and "20%" trace to nothing, so the conclusion fails.
- Right: computations [{"name": "maturities_fy26_fy27", "expr": "D-041 + D-042", "display": "€800 million"}, {"name": "tax_rate", "expr": "-D-043 / D-044", "display": "20.0%"}] and the text "Maturities of €600 million and €200 million total €800 million, and the effective tax rate was 20.0%." The minus sign in "-D-043" is there because the tax expense is reported as a negative number. In the same way, adding back an expense that is reported as a negative number subtracts its id: with D-045 EBIT (expr_value 500000000) and D-046 amortization of acquired intangibles reported as "(40)" (expr_value -40000000), EBIT plus the amortization add-back is "D-045 - D-046", which gives 540000000.

Rules for metrics over several years (a criterion whose label or hint asks for years, such as ROTIC level (10y)):
- <inputs_by_year>, when present, is code's index of the data ids that hold each NOPAT and TICAP line item, one line per company and fiscal year (a balance belongs to the year it closes). Use it to see which years can be computed and to pair the right year-end balances, and read each row's statement in <data> before you use it. Its reported_negative list names the ids whose expr_value is negative: mind their sign in every expr (NOPAT adds acquired-intangible amortization back, so a negative amortization id is subtracted).
- Compute the metric for every fiscal year where its inputs exist in <data>, one declared computation per year, with the definitions in <metrics> (ROTIC = NOPAT / average TICAP, the average of the TICAP at the start and at the end of the fiscal year). The start of fiscal year N is the end of fiscal year N-1, so only average two year-end balances that are one year apart.
- When a component of a definition has no data item (for example no non-interest-bearing current liabilities, or no normalized tax rate), compute the closest proxy from the components you have and say in the text what was left out or replaced (for example the year's effective tax rate in place of a normalized rate). When the start-of-year balance is missing, the year-end TICAP may stand in for the average, and the text says so. Before you call an input missing, look for it in <data> under other names (for example amortization from purchase price allocation (PPA) adjustments is acquired-intangible amortization). Use the same method for every year and every company you compare. Where the method has to differ (a component one company reports and another does not), say so in the text, and never write that the methods are the same when they are not.
- Keep one company's whole series in one conclusion (every yearly computation and the summary), so the summary can use the yearly computations by name.

- A threshold criterion with a numeric bar needs rule_input "<conclusion key>:<computation name>": the computation code compares with the bar. Code recomputes the score from it.
- confidence is data coverage, not a feeling: high when the data covers what the criterion asks, medium when parts are missing, low when much is missing (for example fewer than the ten years a 10-year criterion asks for, or a proxy that leaves out a component).
- The text says the score and why, using only numbers that trace to the cited conclusions' data or computations, the rubric bars, or the scale (-1, 0, +1).

Rules for charts:

conclusions.text: For Siemens Healthineers, EBIT, amortization from IFRS 3 purchase price allocation and the effective tax rate are available for fiscal years 2022 to 2026, and total assets, cash, goodwill and current liabilities for computing TICAP are available at fiscal year-ends 2018, 2019, 2022, 2023, 2025 and 2026. NOPAT is computed as EBIT plus the purchase price allocation amortization add-back (reported as a negative figure) less taxes at the year's effective rate less income attributable to non-controlling interests; no equity income or operating-lease interest component is reported, so neither is included. TICAP is computed as total assets less cash less goodwill, leaving non-interest-bearing current liabilities out because they are not separately disclosed; trade payables are not used because they are not reported at every year-end needed, so TICAP is a proxy of total assets less cash less goodwill. For FY2022, NOPAT is EBIT less the amortization add-back, less tax at the year's effective rate, less non-controlling interest income; FY2022 ROTIC uses FY2022 year-end TICAP alone as a proxy for the average, because FY2021 year-end total assets, cash and goodwill are unavailable; FY2022 ROTIC is 15.1%. For FY2023, NOPAT uses EBIT, the amortization add-back and non-controlling interest income, with average TICAP from FY2022 and FY2023 year-end balances; FY2023 ROTIC is 10.7%. For FY2025, amortization add-back and non-controlling interest data exist but FY2024 total assets, cash and goodwill are missing, so FY2025 ROTIC uses FY2025 year-end TICAP alone as a proxy for the average; FY2025 ROTIC is 16.9%. For FY2026, no purchase price allocation amortization figure is reported for the year, so NOPAT is EBIT less tax at the year's effective rate less non-controlling interest income, with average TICAP from FY2025 and FY2026 year-end balances; FY2026 ROTIC is 15.0%. Across the four fiscal years that could be computed (FY2022, FY2023, FY2025, FY2026), the mean ROTIC is 14.4%.

GE HealthCare's NOPAT is computed as operating income plus amortization of intangible assets less taxes at the year's effective rate, since no equity income, operating-lease interest component or non-controlling interest is given in the data. TICAP is computed as total assets less cash less goodwill less current liabilities net of short-term debt, as a proxy for non-interest-bearing current liabilities, leaving out any non-interest-bearing liabilities not separable from short-term debt. For FY2023, NOPAT uses operating income and amortization, with average TICAP from FY2022 and FY2023 year-end balances; FY2023 ROTIC is 26.8%. For FY2024, NOPAT uses operating income and amortization, with average TICAP from FY2023 and FY2024; FY2024 ROTIC is 26.5%. For FY2025, NOPAT uses operating income and amortization, with average TICAP from FY2024 and FY2025; FY2025 ROTIC is 25.2%. Across the three fiscal years computed, the mean ROTIC is 26.2%.

Philips' NOPAT is computed as operating income plus amortization of intangible assets less taxes at the year's effective rate, since no equity income, operating-lease interest component or non-controlling interest is given in the data; in FY2022 and FY2023 both operating income and the pre-tax income used for the tax rate are negative. TICAP is computed as total assets less cash less goodwill less current liabilities net of short-term debt, as a proxy for non-interest-bearing current liabilities. For FY2023, operating income and amortization are used with an effective tax rate derived from a negative pre-tax income and a negative tax expense; average TICAP uses FY2022 and FY2023 year-end balances; FY2023 ROTIC is 3.8%. For FY2024, operating income and amortization are used, with average TICAP from FY2023 and FY2024; FY2024 ROTIC is -33.4%. For FY2025, operating income and amortization are used, with average TICAP from FY2024 and FY2025; FY2025 ROTIC is 18.1%. Across the three fiscal years computed, the mean ROTIC is -3.8%.

scores.text: Across the four fiscal years that could be computed (FY2022, FY2023, FY2025, FY2026) out of the ten the criterion asks for, SHL's mean ROTIC is 14.4%, close to but just below the 15% threshold for a plus-one score and well above the 10% minus-one bar, so the score is set at the midpoint. Several years (FY2024, and years before FY2022) could not be computed because total assets, cash and goodwill were not all available in the data, and the FY2022 and FY2025 computations use year-end TICAP as a proxy for the average because the prior year-end balance was unavailable, so confidence is low.

On the same proxy method (operating EBIT plus acquired-intangible amortization less tax at the effective rate, over total assets less cash less goodwill and, where available, net of non-interest-bearing current liabilities), SHL's mean ROTIC across FY2022, FY2023, FY2025 and FY2026 is 14.4%, versus GE HealthCare's mean of 26.2% across FY2023-FY2025 and Philips' mean of -3.8% across FY2023-FY2025. SHL's figure is below GE HealthCare's but above Philips', and the three series are not perfectly comparable: GE HealthCare's and Philips' TICAP proxies net current liabilities of short-term debt (not available for SHL), SHL's fiscal year ends three months earlier, and Philips' FY2022-FY2023 figures reflect negative operating income and pre-tax income.
